title: Open base restriction preserves closed relative squares and their diagonals
statement: Let $A,B,C$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] with morphisms $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$, $f:A\to C$ satisfying $q\circ f=p$. Write $D=A\times_C A$, $p_2=p\circ\operatorname{pr}_1:D\to B$ and $\delta:A\to D$ for the diagonal [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to B$, set $A_T=A\times_BT$, $C_T=C\times_BT$, let $f_T:A_T\to C_T$ be induced by $f$, and put $D_T=A_T\times_{C_T}A_T$. There is a canonical isomorphism $D_T\cong D\times_BT$ compatible with both projections to $A$ and with the structure map to $T$; under it the diagonal of $f_T$ is the base change of $\delta$. If $T=W\subseteq B$ is an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], then $A_W$, $C_W$ and $D_W$ identify over $A,C,D$ with the inverse-image open subschemes $p^{-1}(W)$, $q^{-1}(W)$ and $p_2^{-1}(W)$, respectively. Under these identifications the maps $A_W\to W$ and $D_W\to W$ are the restrictions of $p$ and $p_2$. If the underlying maps of $p$ and $p_2$ are closed (send closed subsets to closed subsets), these two restricted maps are closed. For any $h:T\to B$ factoring through $W$, the canonical isomorphisms $A_W\times_WT\cong A\times_BT$ and $C_W\times_WT\cong C\times_BT$ identify the induced morphisms and their diagonals.

proof.text: Write $r_1,r_2:D_T\to A_T$ for the projections, $a_i:D_T\to A$ for their composites, and $t_i:D_T\to T$ for their structure maps. The equality $f_T r_1=f_T r_2$ gives $f a_1=f a_2$ and $t_1=t_2=:t$ by composing with the projections of $C_T$. Thus $(a_1,a_2):D_T\to D$ exists, and $p_2(a_1,a_2)=p a_1=h t$. The fibre-product universal property therefore defines $e=((a_1,a_2),t):D_T\to D\times_B T$. This constructs the comparison and its required projection equations.

source.place: Tag 001V, categories-definition-fibre-products: universal property; explicit comparison needed in Tag 05X9.

proof.text: Conversely, let $d:D\times_B T\to D$ and $t:D\times_B T\to T$ be the projections and put $b_i=\operatorname{pr}_i d$. We have $f b_1=f b_2$ and $p b_i=h t$ (for $i=2$, use $p=qf$). Hence $u_i=(b_i,t):D\times_B T\to A_T$ exist. Their images in $C_T$ agree since both have projections $f b_1=f b_2$ and $t$. This defines $v=(u_1,u_2):D\times_B T\to D_T$. The two composites $ev$ and $ve$ have the identity projections at every fibre product, so uniqueness in the universal property makes them identities. Thus $e$ is the canonical isomorphism, compatible with both maps to $A$ and with the map to $T$. All pairs here denote morphisms defined by universal properties, not pairs of underlying scheme points.

source.place: Tag 001V, categories-definition-fibre-products: uniqueness of the morphism to a fibre product.

proof.text: Let $a:A_T\to A$ and $t:A_T\to T$ be the projections. The diagonal $\delta_T:A_T\to D_T$ has both projections equal to $\mathrm{id}_{A_T}$. Consequently $e\delta_T$ has $D$-projection $(a,a)=\delta a$ and $T$-projection $t$. The base change of $\delta$ is precisely the unique morphism $(\delta a,t):A_T\to D\times_B T$. Their projections coincide, so they are equal. This verifies compatibility of the specified diagonal morphisms.

source.place: Tag 001V, categories-definition-fibre-products; Tag 05X9, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-unramified-universally-injective, proof: base change of the diagonal.

proof.text: Now let $h:W\hookrightarrow B$ be the inclusion of an open subscheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] to $p$, $q$ and $p_2$. It identifies $A\times_B W$, $C\times_B W$ and $D\times_B W$ with $p^{-1}(W)$, $q^{-1}(W)$ and $p_2^{-1}(W)$, with their inclusions and restriction morphisms as the two projections. Combine the last identification with $e$ from steps 1--2 for $T=W$ to identify $D_W$ as well. The asserted maps to $W$ are the restrictions because the cited statement identifies those projections, not merely their sources. The induced map $f_W$ agrees with restriction of $f$: both have $C$-projection $f a$ and the same $W$-projection, and are equal by uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 01JR, schemes-lemma-open-fibre-product, with the second factor an open in the base; Tag 05X9, first sentence of the proof.

proof.text: For $r=p$ or $r=p_2$, let $Z$ be any closed subset of $r^{-1}(W)$. In the subspace topology write $Z=F\cap r^{-1}(W)$ for a closed subset $F$ of the original source. Directly by membership, $r(Z)=r(F)\cap W$. Since $r$ is closed by hypothesis, $r(F)$ is closed in $B$, and its intersection with $W$ is closed in $W$. Therefore the restricted map $r^{-1}(W)\to W$ is closed. Step 4 identifies these with the two maps in the statement. This argument invokes neither universal closedness nor closedness after arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 05X9, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-unramified-universally-injective, proof, first sentence: assumption (2) and (3) survive replacement by an open.

proof.text: Finally write $h=j k$ with $k:T\to W$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow B$. For either $X=A$ or $X=C$ with structure map $s:X\to B$, define $\alpha:(X\times_B W)\times_W T\to X\times_B T$ by $((x,w),t)\mapsto(x,t)$ and $\beta:X\times_B T\to(X\times_B W)\times_W T$ by $(x,t)\mapsto((x,k t),t)$. These are notation for the unique morphisms determined by their projections. The equations $s x=j k t$ and $w=k t$ give their existence and show that their composites have the identity projections, hence are identities. For $X=A,C$, the two possible composites with $f$ both have projections $f x$ and $t$, so $\alpha$ identifies the induced morphisms. The two induced comparisons of relative self-products have the corresponding two $A$-projections; each diagonal has both projections equal to the source identity. Uniqueness therefore identifies their diagonals as well.
